rv.q: Taylor embraces the music of singers from the Righteous Brothers to Mariah Carey, and her all-Black cast and band perform beloved classics and lesser-known oldies with gusto.
Every number in this show gets the audience moving, singing along or both.
Black Ensemble Theatre’s latest production, written and creatively staged by Artistic Director Jackie Taylor, is a toe-tapping, hand-clapping, head-bopping singalong of memorable hits.

While the performance has some areas that need improvement, particularly in the chemistry on stage, delivery of lines, and dancing, which seems a bit basic and off-rhythm, it still impresses with its powerful singing and message of unity.
As a whole, this production is fun, exciting, and uniquely enjoyable.

cn.t: Critics praise Jackie Taylor's musical revue for its powerful vocalists and clever concept of Black performers reclaiming white-written soul songs, though the show works better as a concert than theatrical narrative.
